# Roster — tiers, stats and measurement

*Generated by `eval/gen_roster.js` from the completed re-rating campaign
(66,670 races, ten venues at 600/char — see
[../eval/RATING.md](../eval/RATING.md)). Regenerate after any campaign:*

```sh
node regatta/eval/gen_roster.js
```

## How to use this document

**The `Int` column is yours.** It is the *intended* tier, it is hand-edited, and the
generator preserves it — re-running after a new campaign refreshes every measured column
and leaves your decisions alone. A `·` means no intention has been recorded yet.

`Mea` is the measured tier, assigned by the standing S/A/B/C/D shape (12/21/33/21/13% of
the roster). Where `Int` and `Mea` disagree, that is the balance work queue.

Nothing here is authoritative for the game: `AI_CONFIG` in `js/script.js` remains the only
source of truth for stats. This document is a design surface over it.

---

## Widening the top-to-bottom spread

The roster currently spans **-5.02% to +5.04%** of a
race — a **10.06-point** total range, with
tier means:

| Tier | n | mean rating | mean avg-pts | mean stat budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S** | 12 | -3.81% | 5.686 | 13.4 |
| **A** | 21 | -1.53% | 5.232 | 6.7 |
| **B** | 33 | -0.08% | 4.996 | 2.7 |
| **C** | 21 | +1.58% | 4.618 | -3.9 |
| **D** | 13 | +3.63% | 4.246 | -11.1 |

**S-to-D gap today: 7.44 points of race time**, on a mean stat-budget
difference of **24.5 points**.

The lever is the stat budget, and it is close to linear: rating regresses on total stat
points at **-0.2212% per point** (correlation **-0.844** across the
roster). So widening the S-to-D gap by *G* percentage points of race time needs about
**4.5 × G** points of extra budget separation — split however
you like between raising S and lowering D.

| Target S→D gap | extra budget separation needed |
|---|---|
| 8.9 pts (+1.5) | 7 stat points |
| 9.4 pts (+2) | 9 stat points |
| 10.4 pts (+3) | 14 stat points |
| 11.4 pts (+4) | 18 stat points |

Two cautions before spending it. **Not every stat point costs the same** — `upwind` is the
only stat that pays at all ten venues, `memory` pays at none, and `lightAir` pays only at
swamp. A budget point spent on `memory` widens nothing. See RATING.md for the full
per-venue price table. And **archetypes only subtract**: `corner` and `freight` measure
+2.6 and +2.9 seconds against `bully`, while all four intended-fast archetypes are
indistinguishable from it, so archetype is not currently a lever for lifting the top.

## Notes for the tier rework (2026-08-23)

Worked through against a race simulator built from `rating/ARCHIVE.json` — a character's
time is its measured effect plus `N(0, residSd)` per venue. Validated first: it reproduces
the measured tier points to a mean error of **0.071 points**, so its extrapolations are
usable. Everything below assumes a target of tier mean points **S=7, A=6, B=5, C=4, D=3**.

### That target is self-consistent

Points are zero-sum inside a race, so tier means must average out to the fleet mean.
Weighted by tier size, `(12x7 + 21x6 + 33x5 + 21x4 + 13x3)/100 = 4.98` against a mechanical
fleet mean of ~4.95. It fits.

### ±5 cannot reach it; ±10 can; ±8 cannot

The expressible rating range, accounting for the handling clamp below:

| per-stat range | fastest character | slowest |
|---|---|---|
| ±5 (today) | −11.45% | +11.12% |
| ±8 | −17.66% | +16.99% |
| **±10** | **−21.57%** | **+20.91%** |

At ±5 the S and D tiers run off the end of the scale — the best the current range can do is
about **S 6.7 / D 3.2**, and only by pinning every S character to +5 on all ten stats, which
turns the tier into clones. **±10 is roughly the minimum workable range**; ±8 falls about 1.4
points short of S. Note ±10 gives −21.57%, not a naive doubling to −22.90%, because handling
saturates.

### Preserving character shape makes the target EASIER, not harder

A first pass compressed the performance stats to fit and produced near-identical S
characters. That was a modelling error. **Points are concave in rating**: inside a tier the
weaker half loses more than the stronger half gains, so a tier with real internal spread
lands *lower* than a flat one at the same mean rating — and therefore needs *less* rating to
hit a given points target.

Assuming a flat tier said S needed a budget of **+82**. Keeping every character's real shape
needs **+47**. Roughly half. Identity is not in tension with the target.

### Code constraints found in script.js — read before authoring

- **`AI_STAT_BONUS = 4`** (`script.js:11649`) adds a flat +4 to all seven *performance*
  stats of every AI boat at construction. The physics already sees `authored + 4`, i.e.
  −1..+9 today. It is constant across characters so it does not bias the measured prices,
  but it puts the clamps closer than the authored numbers suggest.
- **`handling` saturates at authored +6.** Five sites consume it as
  `clamp((handling + 4) / 10, 0, 1)`, which hits 1.0 at authored +6 and 0.0 at authored −4.
  Only the `tackAgility` term keeps responding outside that band. So handling above +6 is
  largely wasted, and **handling below −4 is already dead today** — a −5 sails as a −4.
  If handling should keep separating strong characters, that clamp has to move too.
- **`lightAir`, `heavyAir` and `memory` do not take the bonus** and price at ~0 almost
  everywhere: together they are 0.92% of the 11.45% maximum — 8% of the effect for 30% of
  the budget. That makes them the natural home for character identity and venue
  specialisation during a tier-wide power raise, since moving them costs nothing against
  the target.

### The cheaper lever is race noise

Character spread averages **7.7 s against 40.3 s of within-race residual**. Finishing
position is mostly the day, not the boat, which is the real reason points sit in a tight
band around 5. Holding every stat exactly as authored today and only shrinking the residual:

| noise × | S | A | B | C | D | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 | 5.63 | 5.23 | 4.96 | 4.66 | 4.27 | 1.36 |
| 0.50 | 6.22 | 5.50 | 4.98 | 4.39 | 3.71 | 2.51 |
| **0.25** | **7.05** | **5.90** | **5.00** | **3.98** | **2.91** | **4.14** |

Quarter noise hits the target with no stat changes at all. Halving the noise moves the tiers
about as far as tripling every budget.

### Worked example — the current S tier at ±10

One transform, no compression:

> `newStat = round(oldStat + 4.5)` on the seven performance stats, handling capped at +6,
> conditional stats untouched.

Simulated result across all five tiers: **6.92 / 6.13 / 5.07 / 3.85 / 2.69** against
7/6/5/4/3 — S on target, C and D slightly over-scaled and wanting a touch less.

| Character | acc | mom | han | upw | rea | dwn | prs | lgt | hvy | mem | Bud | Rating | Pts |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Talon | +10 | +1 | +6 | +10 | +9 | +2 | +8 | +1 | +1 | 0 | +48 | −15.1% | 7.11 |
| Stomp | +10 | +2 | +6 | +8 | +7 | +5 | +6 | 0 | +1 | 0 | +45 | −13.8% | 6.85 |
| Muninn | +7 | +2 | +6 | +8 | +8 | +3 | +10 | +2 | −1 | +5 | +50 | −14.5% | 7.01 |
| Cruz | +7 | +7 | +6 | +7 | +7 | +7 | +7 | +1 | +1 | +3 | +53 | −14.6% | 6.99 |
| Hug | +2 | +6 | +5 | +10 | +7 | +7 | +10 | +1 | −2 | −5 | +41 | −15.0% | 7.00 |
| Seam | +6 | +1 | +6 | +9 | +6 | +2 | +8 | +4 | −4 | +1 | +39 | −13.0% | 6.78 |
| Chroma | +5 | +5 | +6 | +4 | +6 | +6 | +9 | +5 | −4 | −5 | +37 | −12.7% | 6.78 |
| Pebble | +3 | +10 | +6 | +10 | +1 | +9 | +3 | −1 | +4 | +5 | +50 | −13.0% | 6.76 |
| Puff | +7 | +9 | +6 | +6 | +7 | +2 | +9 | +5 | −3 | +2 | +50 | −14.2% | 7.04 |
| Cheer | +7 | +3 | +6 | +6 | +3 | +4 | +10 | +2 | −1 | −1 | +39 | −12.8% | 6.81 |
| Fathom | +5 | +10 | 0 | +8 | +9 | +9 | +7 | 0 | +5 | +5 | +58 | −14.3% | 6.99 |
| Mistral | +10 | +10 | +6 | +5 | +4 | +5 | +4 | +3 | +3 | +2 | +52 | −13.0% | 6.87 |

Mean budget **+46.8**, mean rating **−13.84%** — well inside the ±100 ceiling. Shape is
preserved rather than compressed: within-character spread across the seven performance stats
goes 7.1 → 7.2, and between-character budget sd goes 5.9 → 6.3. Cruz stays the flat
metronome, Hug keeps the tier's lowest acceleration (her beat line still reads true), Fathom
stays the handling liability.

**Ten of the twelve land on handling +6** — the clamp, not a choice. Handling stops
differentiating strong characters until that limit moves.

### The caveat that is still open

**Every price above +5 is an extrapolation.** No character has ever carried a stat higher
than 5, so the per-point prices beyond that are unverified. The physics supports linearity —
`upwind * 0.012`, `reach * 0.018`, `pressure * 0.05`, `acceleration * 0.024` are plain
multipliers with no clamp in range, and at authored +10 the effective +14 leaves `momMod` at
0.72 and `accelMod` at 1.34 — but supported is not verified. Race a handful of synthetic
characters at +8/+10 across two or three venues before authoring 100 against the new scale.

## Beat lines

Each character's authored counter. Three currently contradict the measurement outright and
are flagged; see the beat-line audit in RATING.md for the full eight.

| Name | Beat line |
|---|---|
| **Talon** | Take him downwind — all that height is worth nothing with the wind behind. |
| **Stomp** | Refuse the brawl and outlast him — stomping bleeds speed. |
| **Muninn** | Run him downwind — memory is worth nothing on water he has not learned. |
| **Cruz** | Nothing to exploit — get ahead early, because he has no burst to take it back. |
| **Hug** | Get ahead early — Hug finishes everything she starts, slowly. |
| **Seam** | Wait for it to blow — she reads the light stuff beautifully and drowns above sixteen knots. |
| **Chroma** | Push her into heavy air — the thinking stops working above sixteen knots. |
| **Pebble** | Reach across her line — precision cannot fix a slow reach. |
| **Puff** | Attack downwind — the dragonet will not run with you. |
| **Cheer** | Out-spike her steady beat — she has no pace off the wind. |
| **Fathom** | Turn the race into corners — momentum cannot help him there. |
| **Mistral** | Fast everywhere — beat the swift on shifts, not speed. |
| **Lure** | Refuse the bait upwind — the runs are a free pass. |
| **Latch** | Break the tow — nobody has ever seen him accelerate on his own. |
| **Flaunt** | Sail your own race — every trick she has costs her when the breeze gets up. |
| **Razor** | No weak stat — refuse the fight and race your own boat. |
| **Zeffir** | Hold him off downwind — gulls glide everywhere but there. |
| **Crush** | Everything between corners is yours — especially the runs. |
| **Torrent** | Absorb the opening surge — the swordfish dulls by leg two. |
| **Glide** | Perfect upwind, lost downwind — make the runs count. |
| **Ember** | Make the race long — the firefish spends everything in the first minute. |
| **Wobble** | Ignores the wind to get there — sail the middle and collect. |
| **Piper** | Take her downwind and stretch — precision is worth nothing on an empty run. |
| **Sovereign** | Sail on his wind — grandeur does not survive being covered. |
| **Bixby** | Beat him to the top mark — upwind he is merely mortal. |
| **Blaze** | Skip the fight, win the runs — makos idle downwind. |
| **Riffle** | Wait for a windy day — she is quick and clever until it blows, then she is just small. |
| **Rift** | Pull away on the runs — eels do not surf. |
| **Ribbon** | Take her air — she needs a clean lane and will not fight you for one. |
| **Regal** | Race the runs — royalty will not hoist and hustle. |
| **Needle** | Take him downwind — the precision that wins him marks is worth nothing on a run. |
| **Torch** | Let the fire burn out — he keeps nothing through lulls or turns. |
| **Prism** | Bury him at the start — a clam that has to accelerate is a clam you have beaten. |
| **Saffron** | She bets it all on the reaches — win the beats and it is over. |
| **Zing** | Survive the launch — the beats bring him back to you. |
| **Dart** | Point high and turn often — darts only fly straight. |
| **Pearl** | Make her tack — every stop costs a fortune in pearls. |
| **Bulkhead** | Hoist and go — the bulkhead sinks on every run. |
| **Stripes** | Give him no errors — the tiger has no plan of his own. |
| **Torpedo** | Take him somewhere new — the pike is only lethal on water he already knows. |
| **Breeze** | Crowd her at starts and marks — slow to build speed, easy to pin. |
| **Spar** | Attack at every mark — he rounds wide and cannot turn back inside you. |
| **Ripple** | Drag her into traffic — clean lanes are where she lives. |
| **Anvil** | Beat him off the line — the hammer needs a lane before it is worth anything. |
| **Sable** | Crowd her — she sails a clean lane or none at all, and dirty air undoes her. |
| **Chisel** | Make him manoeuvre — he has no way of finding that speed again. |
| **Spike** | Point high and stay clear of the horn — he cannot climb after you. |
| **Pinch** | Stay clean upwind, then walk away downwind — he parks there. |
| **Scoop** | Rush the starts and reaches — the pelican needs a runway. |
| **Slipstream** | Deny the tow upwind, then leave — salmon cannot run downstream. |
| **Petal** | Win the beats — the spoonbill blooms only at the marks. |
| **Popper** | Point higher and let him puff himself out. |
| **Finley** | Break cover downwind — his speed lives on the beat. |
| **Strut** | Push her into maneuvers — every turn costs her the strut. |
| **Jester** | Escape upwind — the joke is on him above the layline. |
| **Brine** | Break his rhythm at the marks — restarts are agony for a manatee. |
| **Paddle** | Wait for it to blow — the duck is a puddle sailor at heart. |
| **Flare** | Let him pick the fight, then leave downwind — that is exactly where he is slowest. |
| **Whiskers** | Attack every rounding and reach — the train needs straight track. |
| **Bruce** | Force restarts and tacking duels — he cannot get moving again. |
| **Skerry** | Give him no gaps to thread — then climb away upwind. |
| **Etienne** | Race him in open water — the crawdad only understands a narrow channel. |
| **Sunshine** | Keep her in lulls and dirty air — no gusts, no shine. |
| **Flicker** | Follow the fleet, not the tern — his corner rarely pays. |
| **Tiny** | Just point at the mark — anything above a breeze blows the krill away. |
| **Snap** | Keep him turning — snappers lose their grip in maneuvers. |
| **Skim** | Survive her start, then turn hard and often — she hates corners. |
| **Gasket** | Match him upwind, pull away when the spinnakers go up. |
| **Skip** | Make it a long leg — he spends everything in ten seconds and has nothing left to carry. |
| **Crimson** | Break away in a straight line — he only shines in puffs. |
| **Chomp** | Tack early, tack often — the ambusher cannot follow through turns. |
| **Frond** | Pin him at the start — the seadragon blooms late, downwind. |
| **Croak** | Race him when it honks — the bullfrog only sings in a whisper. |
| **Roll** | Slow him leaving marks — perfect turns, painful exits. |
| **Snag** | Force him to turn — a tacking duel is the one thing he cannot answer. |
| **Bramble** | Stay out of reach — alone, the urchin barely moves. |
| **Clutch** | Do not engage — sail past while he is busy starting fights. |
| **Plunge** | Race him in a drifter — he needs wind to throw himself at, and dies without it. |
| **Nimbus** | Chase him downwind — clouds stall when the wind goes aft. |
| **Anchor** | Own the beats — the turtle only wins races run downhill. |
| **Frenzy** | Keep it tidy — with nothing to bite, the piranha simply drifts. |
| **Wiggle** | Make him steer — wiggling is not turning. |
| **Vex** | Lean on him mid-leg — away from corners he is out of tricks. |
| **Tangle** | Dive downwind — the trap-setter unravels on the runs. |
| **Scuttle** | Deny the chaos — in a clean race he is just slow. |
| **Flash** | Send him upwind — the sprinter's compass only points down. |
| **Lateen** | Send her upwind — a sail she cannot trim is no use against the breeze. |
| **Lunker** | Wait for a light day — he needs pressure to move, and he cannot turn when it arrives. |
| **Drift** | Every maneuver hurts him — force gybes and watch him wilt. |
| **Bluff** | Just point higher — Bluff bluffs; the upwind legs call it. |
| **Splat** | Just race — his corner needs a miracle and a tailwind. |
| **Pulse** | Break away off the wind — sticky feet, short hops. |
| **Dozer** | Put a lap on him early — the nurse shark needs the whole race to get going. |
| **Skitter** | Wait for the breeze to fill — the mudskipper needs a drifter to matter. |
| **Knot** | Sail into pressure — the nautilus cannot cash a gust. |
| **Grip** | Sail around him — he cannot follow, and he was never going to. |
| **Bloom** | Put a beat in front of her — she goes where the wind goes and cannot fight upwind. |
| **Viper** | Slip the cover in open water — he fades on the long legs. |
| **Veil** | Force maneuvers — the cloak tears in every tack. |
| **Splash** | Never let him start a run in front — everywhere else he is a barge. |
